tier_rationale: Polar operates a real vendor cloud (Polar Flow, described on Polar's own product page as 'an online training and workout analysis platform') and the H10's firmware updates are delivered only through the Polar Beat or Polar Flow app -- Polar's own support content states 'To receive the firmware updates, your H10 heart rate sensor needs to be paired with the Polar Beat or Polar Flow app.' That is a vendor cloud this device can use, which rules out D1 under this project's rule that any usable vendor cloud caps the tier at D2, however avoidable it is. Core function -- broadcasting live heart rate over open Bluetooth LE and ANT+ to any receiving watch, bike computer, or third-party app -- needs no app and no account: Polar's own FAQ describes the H10 as usable 'as a standalone device' paired directly from a receiving device's own sensor menu. Vendor cloud exists, setup for core function requires no account, and core function works fully unconnected -- the D2 row, the same shape as the Garmin HRM 200 already in this catalog.
the_unplug_test: The strap keeps broadcasting your heart rate over Bluetooth LE and ANT+ to anything listening -- a sports watch, a bike computer, gym equipment, any of the 150+ compatible third-party apps -- with no phone nearby and no Polar account ever created. Pairing to a receiving device is done from that device's own sensor menu, no app required. The only things gated behind the Polar Beat or Polar Flow app are optional: training analysis, and firmware updates, which the sensor cannot receive without pairing to one of Polar's own apps.
offline_losses: firmware updates, which Polar's support documentation states require pairing to the Polar Beat or Polar Flow app
onboard training-session recording and analysis via Polar Flow (the H10 can record one session, up to 30 hours, in internal memory, but retrieving/analyzing it is a Polar Flow/Beat function)

repairability.notes: User-replaceable CR2025 coin cell; Polar publishes a battery-replacement how-to video. Sensor module is separate from the washable fabric strap.

sources.supports: Official Polar product page and FAQ: confirms Bluetooth LE and ANT 2.1 dual connectivity, describes the H10 as usable 'both as a standalone device and pair it with various fitness apps, sports watches and smart watches' and compatible with 'over 150' third-party apps; describes Polar Flow as 'an online training and workout analysis platform.' Tech specs: coin-cell battery rated up to 400h, WR30 (30m) water resistance, one-session/30-hour onboard recording, 21g sensor weight, and a FAQ entry confirming the CR2025 coin cell is user-replaceable ('It's easy to replace it with a new CR2025 coin cell battery').

Full grant list for grantee Polar Electro Oy (code INW) showing the vendor files FCC grants for its Bluetooth heart rate sensors generally (H7i, H6, and two unnamed 'Heart Rate Sensor'/'Heart Rate Sensor module' grants dated 2017-2018 whose timing matches the H10's 2018 launch, though no exhibit title in the search results explicitly names 'H10'). Establishes INW as a grantee that files for this exact product category.

Polar's own H10 support page: 'You'll be able to update the firmware via the Polar Beat or Polar Flow mobile app' — establishing that firmware updates route through a Polar app backed by Polar's cloud, which is what caps this at D2 rather than D1. The same page confirms the strap is compatible with ANT+ and standard Bluetooth, so any watch or third-party app can receive heart rate with no Polar account involved — which is why core function is untouched and it is D2 rather than lower.

open_questions: The exact FCC ID covering the H10 specifically was not pinned down within budget -- two unnamed 2017/2018 grants under Polar's INW grantee code (INW2L, INW2R) are timing-plausible candidates but their manual exhibits were not read to confirm.
Price in current US dollars was not confirmed within budget (Polar's own page showed EUR 99.90; a USD MSRP figure was not independently verified) -- left null rather than guessed.
Whether a firmware update, once started, can be declined or is forced was not established.
notes: Direct cross-vendor parallel to garmin-hrm-200: same subcategory, same D2 tier, same reasoning (broadcast function is open and standalone; a real vendor cloud exists but only touches optional app-based features). Useful for a reader comparing brands, since the tier outcome is identical despite Polar and Garmin being separate ecosystems -- the chest-strap heart-rate-monitor category as a whole appears to have converged on this shape rather than offering a true D1 option among mainstream vendors.

local_replacement_note: No documented third-party tool replaces Polar Flow's session analysis or the firmware-update path; core broadcast function never depends on either.
